title: Home practical guide and safety card: fizzing balloon
subject: Science
unit: Spring 2: Changes of materials and animals including humans
source: Written for science/y5 lesson 21 (Home practical guide and safety card: fizzing balloon (portal worksheet; over a tray, adult present, never seal tightly))
intro: Lesson 21: Irreversible changes: making new materials. A practical to do at home with an adult nearby. Read it all first.

practical.aim: To see a new material (a gas) being made
safety: An adult knows what you are doing and is nearby
Clear a space and tidy up afterwards; wash your hands
method: Work over a tray with an adult
Pour about 3 cm of vinegar into the bottle
Use the funnel to put two spoons of bicarbonate of soda into the balloon
Stretch the balloon over the bottle neck, then lift it so the powder falls in
Watch the balloon; never seal the bottle tightly with a lid
Record what happens and say if the change is reversible

questions.q: Big question: can you unbake a cake?
questions.a: No: baking makes new materials, so it is irreversible.
